hook: AI gave me a 6-paragraph essay when I needed a yes or a no.
caption:
AI gave me a 6-paragraph essay when I needed a yes or a no.

You asked: "Should I launch this as a subscription or one-time purchase?"

AI responded with the history of SaaS pricing, three frameworks, a pros/cons table, and the phrase "ultimately, it depends on your goals."

Cool. Super helpful. Very yes or no.

Here's what's actually happening: the AI doesn't know if you're a researcher who wants every angle, or a decision-maker who needs a call and a reason. So it hedges. It covers all bases. It buries the answer in padding because it's guessing at what kind of thinker you are.

Some people genuinely want the 6 paragraphs. They'll feel cheated without the nuance.

Some people see 6 paragraphs and their brain exits the building.

Neither is wrong. The AI just doesn't know which one you are — so it writes for everyone, which means it writes for no one.

BootFile fixes this by building a profile of how you actually process information. Direct or exploratory. Big picture first or details first. Options or recommendations.

Once it knows you, "yes or no" questions finally get yes or no answers.

With a reason. One reason.
